problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2x\sqrt{y},\,y(1)=4
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method. What entry should be placed in the column for $Δy$ in the second row of the table below if the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{2}?$ Do not round the answer.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $4$ | $4$ | $2$ |
| $$ | $$ | $$ | {{field-1}} |
worked_solution:
To get the values of $x$ and $y$ in the second row, we add $Δx$ to $x$ and $Δy$ to $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx \\  & =1+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & =4+2 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $4$ | $4$ | $2$ |
| $\frac{3}{2}$ | $6$ | $$ | $$ |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule (using the values of $x$ and $y$ in the second row), and we compute 
$Δy$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =2x\sqrt{y} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot \sqrt{6} \\ Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =3\sqrt{6}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{6}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $4$ | $4$ | $2$ |
| $\frac{3}{2}$ | $6$ | $3\sqrt{6}$ | $\frac{3\sqrt{6}}{2}$ |
